messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - us-west2 inference cluster error spike. Autoscaler saw repeated rapid scale-up/scale-down (thrash) over the last 8m, resulting in container crashloops and CUDA OOMs on several hosts. Paging @Maya S. (oncall).

Maya S.: I'm on it. seeing ~30% 5xxs for hosted-generation in us-west2, tail latency skyrocketing. Any auto-remediations already triggered?

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale_event: up -> 40 nodes (2024-05-12T14:01:10Z), scale_event: down -> 18 nodes (2024-05-12T14:03:30Z), repeat x3.

Liam R.: Confirmed crashloops on runtime pods; logs show repeated CUDA OOMs during KV cache restore. Likely unsafe concurrent restores during rapid pod churn.

Maya S.: Can you paste the OOM trace?

Liam R.: ```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 26.12 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 3.34 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  at /workspace/runtime/launch.cpp:line 482
  kernel: attention_forward
```

Kai T.: Nodes are flapping between Ready and NotReady because pods creating at high rate + eviction. kubelet logs show docker/containerd restarts due to OOM and then image pull pressure.

Maya S.: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Pause autoscaler burst/scale-down to stop thrash. 2) Manually stabilize at current capacity to drain unhealthy pods. 3) Route new traffic to eu-central warm region for critical customers. 4) Enable model fallback to quantized variant for hosted tier.

Maya S.: Executing step 1 now: updating autoscaler policy to set cooldown 600s and max-scale-down-rate 10%.

Kai T.: Command I ran to pause burst: ```kubectl patch hpa inference-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":600}}}}'```

Evan (eng-sre): I'll cordon the three most-affected nodes and drain pods to avoid further restarts. Cordon nodes: node-uw2-gpu-17/18/21.

Ashley (CSE): Heads up — two mid-market customers reported degraded throughput and increased 504s. One is on a heavy streaming workload. I'm going to open a support note and offer temporary routing to eu-central if needed.

Maya S.: Routing change: updating gateway routing rules to prefer eu-central for orgs tagged critical. Pushing config now.

deploy-bot: gateway: route-update applied to service/user-gen: prefer eu-central for tags [enterprise,critical] (2024-05-12T14:10:05Z).

Liam R.: Additional mitigation: disable KV cache restores on cold start for new pods to reduce memory spike. Patching runtime config to lazy-kv-restore=true.

Maya S.: Patching runtime config (rolling restart) for inference deployment to enable lazy-kv-restore. Command: ```kubectl set env deployment/inference-runtime LAZY_KV_RESTORE=true --namespace=us-west2 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-runtime --namespace=us-west2```

Liam R.: Also enabling an interim admission controller limit to prevent scheduling very large-model requests on newly-created nodes. This will force smaller-model fallback for the next 15m while cluster stabilizes.

Kai T.: Drains complete on node-uw2-gpu-17/18/21. Nodes cordoned. Observed immediate reduction in restarts.

Evan (eng-sre): Manually scaled statefulsets to 22 nodes worth of capacity and disabled autoscaler for 10m to observe. Command: ```kubectl scale --replicas=22 sts/inference-workers --namespace=us-west2```

Maya S.: Good. Metrics look better: error rate down from 30% -> 8% in last 6m, avg latency decreased. Still seeing a few OOMs on old pods. Monitoring memory pressure.

Ashley (CSE): I've notified affected customers: 2 reported, one accepted routing to eu-central and saw immediate improvement. They've asked for an incident summary afterwards.

Liam R.: Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler config allowed aggressive downscaling during transient L7 drops; combined with warmup-time for large models (KV restore) caused multiple pods to attempt full restore concurrently leading to memory overcommit on noisy nodes. Need autoscaler damping and pre-warm logic.

Maya S.: Agreed. Follow-up actions (post-incident): 1) Add stabilization window to autoscaler defaults 2) Add rate-limiter to KV restores (stagger) 3) Add node-level memory reservation and guardrail to admission 4) Test in staging under synthetic burst workloads.

Evan (eng-sre): I'll file the incident with preliminary impact numbers and assign follow-ups: IRC-2024-045. Preliminary customer impact: ~0.7% of all requests returned 5xx during the 18m spike, affecting 14 orgs with at least one customer-visible error.

Maya S.: Handoff: I'm going to sleep-share the oncall to Kai T. for monitoring & follow-up while I triage config changes and write the postmortem. Kai, you're now the primary oncall for this thread.

Kai T.: Taking over. I'll keep the autoscaler paused and monitor for 30m, then coordinate a controlled re-enable with a higher stabilization window. Please DM me if anything new pops up.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: behavior updated: stabilizationWindowSeconds=600; burst disabled (2024-05-12T14:21:10Z).

Maya S.: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident timeline and assign the follow-ups to runtime/infra/sre. Estimated P1->P2 reduction target: ensure no recurrence in the next 1 week under load tests.

Ashley (CSE): Adding note to support ticket: customers routed or impacted, we're offering credits for failed requests and a post-incident call if they want one.

Liam R.: Extra: we should add a canary that starts with a smaller KV cache to warm before full restore. I'll prototype in staging.

Evan (eng-sre): Logged follow-ups in IRC-2024-045: [autoscaler defaults], [kv-restore-stagger], [node-guardrails], [customer-comms].

Kai T.: Monitoring OK for now, I'll re-enable controlled autoscaling at +30m with stabilizationWindowSeconds=600 and max-scale-down-rate=5%. If anything regresses I'll page.

Maya S.: Thanks. Marking this thread as active/handed-off. Will follow up with postmortem draft in ~24h. :thumbsup:
